I'll read `PR.diff` and the related source in this workspace, then report findings by severity with file:line citations.Next I'll read the updated `brief.ts` parser and how turn-end wiring applies empty ask lists.Checking a few edge cases the widened regex may mishandle:## Review findings

### Major — `brief.ts:421` — `waiting on/for` only checks the next token
`NO_ASK` uses `(?!(?:your?|dave)\b)` only on the word immediately after `on`/`for`. Phrases that still wait on Dave are treated as no-ask and become `[]`, which `mergeParsed` uses to wipe prior asks and drop `waiting-on-dave`:

- `Waiting for confirmation from Dave`
- `Waiting for a decision from you`
- `Waiting on sign-off from you`

That conflicts with the stated rule (exclude waits on you/Dave) and is stronger than a display glitch: model prose can clear real open asks.

### Major — `brief.ts:421` — `none\b(?!\s+of\b)` is far broader than the old separator form
Old `NONE_ITEM` required `None` plus a separator or end (`—`, `:`, `.`, etc.). The new pattern treats almost any line that starts with `None` (except `None of…`) as no-ask. Items that still ask Dave are dropped / clear the list, e.g.:

- `None until you confirm the branch`
- `None land without your LGTM`

A sole such item returns `[]` and clears earlier asks (same path as P26/E14c).

### Major — `brief.ts:421` — prefix alts match even when the rest still asks Dave
These branches match at the start of the line and ignore the rest:

- `nothing\s+(?:…|needed|required|yet|for\s+now)\b`
- `no\s+(?:action|input|reply)\s+(?:needed|required)\b`

So e.g. `Nothing needed except your approval` and `No action needed until you reply` are no-ask, produce `[]`, and clear open asks even though Dave still owes an action. The `?` guard does not help unless a `?` is present.

### Minor — `brief.ts:437` — unbulleted no-ask prose now clears asks
Previously only unbulleted `none…` set `none`. Now any unbulleted `NO_ASK` hit (e.g. bare `Waiting on the CI run.` under `## Next steps`) yields `[]`. Easy for free-prose Next steps to wipe asks without a list item.

### Minor — `brief.ts:423` — ask forced only on ASCII `?`
`noAsk` uses `text.includes('?')`. A fullwidth `？` (or similar) does not force an ask, so a wait-on-Dave line that uses it can still be classified no-ask and clear state.

---

Skipped (nothing new in this diff): fail-open paths, missed events, pagination, partial writes. Empty `ask: []` is handled correctly for clearing (`[]` is truthy in `mergeParsed` / `learnFromAnswer`).
